nodes.title: Migration Expand/Contract
nodes.summary: Use backward-compatible schema phases, dual-tolerant readers and writers, bounded backfill, reconciliation, and delayed destructive cleanup. This keeps mixed-version deployments and rollback safe.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the migration sequence, compatibility matrix, deployment gates, dual-read/write metrics, backfill checkpointing, reconciliation evidence, and the explicit approval or gate for destructive contract cleanup. Confirm that a rollback to the previous application version remains compatible at every intermediate schema state.

nodes.title: Bounded Backfill
nodes.summary: Run migrations in stable-key, idempotent batches with durable checkpoints, throttling, and explicit pause, retry, and abort controls. This prevents resource exhaustion and makes restart safe.
nodes.probe: Parse migration and backfill jobs for a stable key-range or cursor, bounded batch size, persisted checkpoint, retry handling, and rate or lock controls, rejecting an unbounded full-table transaction. In staging, interrupt the job between batches and assert that restart resumes from the checkpoint without duplicate or missing changes.

nodes.title: Migration Rollback or Forward Fix
nodes.summary: Provide a tested reversible down path or an explicitly safe forward fix for every migration, including compatibility and data-loss boundaries. This keeps partial schema changes recoverable.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the migration's down script or forward-fix runbook, interruption tests, compatibility matrix, data-loss declaration, and evidence that operators can execute it under the deployment system's permissions. Reject a generic “restore backup” plan that does not account for writes made after the migration.

nodes.title: Migration Lock Safety
nodes.summary: Use online or concurrent DDL, short transactions, and explicit lock and statement timeouts, with production-sized preflight estimates. This bounds blocking and prevents live-traffic lock cascades.
nodes.probe: Parse migration SQL and database settings for online or concurrent operations, lock and statement timeouts, and bounded transaction scopes, rejecting table rewrites or unbounded DDL without an approved exception. Rehearse the migration under concurrent load and confirm a timeout releases the waiting session.

nodes.title: Migration Schema Drift
nodes.summary: Treat migration history as the schema authority and compare clean and deployed databases against normalized expected DDL. This detects manual changes, missing migrations, and altered history before they affect operations.
nodes.probe: Create a disposable database, apply every migration, dump normalized DDL, and diff it against the checked-in schema snapshot and recorded production migration version. Fail if production contains unmanaged objects or if a migration checksum differs from the deployed history.

nodes.title: Migration Deployment Order
nodes.summary: Ensure additive schema changes precede application rollout and contract cleanup follows an explicit drain gate for old binaries and consumers. This protects rolling deploys and rollback compatibility.
nodes.probe: Parse the CI/CD DAG and release manifests to verify expand migrations precede application rollout and contract migrations require an explicit later gate after old versions are drained. Exercise a rolling deployment with one old worker and assert it remains functional during the overlap window.

nodes.title: Migration Rehearsal
nodes.summary: Rehearse high-risk migrations on a production-sized, representative clone under realistic concurrency and traffic while measuring locks, WAL, lag, and recovery behavior. This exposes production-scale failure modes before approval.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the clone's scale and data-shape rationale, exact artifact identity, concurrency workload, resource measurements, abort/recovery exercise, and dated sign-off. A small developer database or a timing-only run is insufficient evidence.

nodes.title: Migration Reconciliation
nodes.summary: Gate cutover by comparing old and new representations with key sets, counts, hashes, null/error rates, and business invariants. This turns backfill completion into an evidence-based decision.
nodes.probe: Run the repository reconciliation command against old and new representations and fail when primary-key sets, counts, hashes, or invariant-query results differ beyond an explicit threshold. Include a deliberately corrupted fixture to verify the command returns nonzero and identifies the affected partition or key range.

nodes.title: Backup RPO and Retention
nodes.summary: Configure automated backups and change-log retention to meet written RPO, RTO, and restore-window targets. The policy defines usable recovery-point frequency, lifetime, and recovery location.
nodes.probe: Present the exact decision: “What are the maximum acceptable committed data loss, service restoration time, and historical restore window?” Require options in numeric units (RPO: 0, ≤5 minutes, ≤1 hour, >1 hour; RTO: ≤15 minutes, ≤1 hour, ≤4 hours, >4 hours; restore window: 7, 30, 90, or 365+ days), plus an owner and written exception for any other value.

nodes.title: Backup Restore Drill
nodes.summary: Periodically restore a real backup into an isolated environment, start the exact application artifact, and exercise representative reads and writes while measuring recovery. This validates usable recovery rather than backup-job success alone.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect dated drill records showing the selected backup, isolated target, exact application/version, startup and representative workflow results, measured restore time and recovery point, defects, and remediation. A provider “backup succeeded” metric alone is not evidence.

nodes.title: Backup Integrity Check
nodes.summary: Verify backup manifests, checksums, metadata, and WAL or change-log continuity before marking an artifact usable. Automatic evidence must identify incomplete, corrupted, or tampered recovery chains.
nodes.probe: For PostgreSQL base backups, run `pg_verifybackup` and validate the required WAL segment range; for the selected provider, parse backup-verification status and fail on missing checksum or manifest evidence. Include a negative fixture with a missing WAL segment and assert it is rejected.

nodes.title: Point-in-Time Recovery Capability
nodes.summary: Continuously archive WAL or equivalent change logs and prove recovery to arbitrary timestamps within the retention horizon. This bounds data loss to the committed recovery-point objective.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect archive configuration, continuity/lag alerts, retention horizon, and a recent drill that restored to an arbitrary timestamp and verified which known writes were present or absent. Evidence must demonstrate the declared RPO, not just snapshot availability.

nodes.title: Backup Access Isolation
nodes.summary: Encrypt backups in transit and at rest, isolate their destination from the primary trust boundary, and restrict restore access to least-privilege break-glass identities. This preserves recoverability during compromise.
nodes.probe: Parse infrastructure and provider backup settings for encryption keys, TLS transfer, an isolated or immutable destination, retention lock, and a separate restore role, failing when any required control is absent. Verify the production application role cannot list, delete, or restore backup objects.

nodes.title: Backup Erasure Policy
nodes.summary: Reconcile retention, legal holds, subject erasure, snapshots, logs, replicas, exports, and expiry into an owned policy. The policy states what remains recoverable and how holds override ordinary deletion.
nodes.probe: Present the exact decision: “When a subject-erasure request conflicts with a backup retention or legal hold, which policy applies?” Options: (A) delete/sanitize eligible backup copies immediately, (B) retain backups until expiry but suppress on restore and document completion, (C) legal hold overrides erasure until a named release date, or (D) another reviewed policy with owner and date. Require evidence of enforcement for every backup/log class.

nodes.title: Restore Consistency Checks
nodes.summary: Keep a restored or promoted database isolated until referential integrity, uniqueness, sequences, checksums or counts, and critical aggregates pass. Fail closed when logical consistency is not proven.
nodes.probe: Run a versioned post-restore SQL suite that checks constraint violations, orphan counts, primary-key uniqueness, sequence high-water marks, and selected aggregate totals, returning nonzero on any failure. Confirm endpoint promotion is blocked when the suite fails.

nodes.title: Replication Topology
nodes.summary: Document the authoritative writer, eligible standbys and replicas, replication modes, regions, quorum, and each link's recovery and consistency contract. This makes failover authority and stale-read behavior explicit.
nodes.probe: Present the exact decision: “Which database is authoritative for writes, which replicas may be promoted, and what consistency/RPO contract applies to each read path?” Options: single writer with async replicas; synchronous quorum across regions; provider-managed multi-zone writer/standby; or another documented topology. Require named endpoints, promotion authority, lag thresholds, and owner.

nodes.title: Replication Lag Freshness
nodes.summary: Measure replication byte and time lag and use explicit freshness thresholds to gate reads, jobs, and promotion. A connected replica that exceeds its contract is unavailable for that use.
nodes.probe: Query database or provider replication metrics, alert when byte or time lag exceeds the configured threshold, and verify in an integration probe that the router refuses stale replicas. Inject or simulate lag and assert promotion is blocked at the declared RPO boundary.

nodes.title: Failover Runbook
nodes.summary: Maintain a versioned executable procedure for detection, fencing, promotion, endpoint and secret rotation, pool draining, verification, and return to service. It assigns authority, stop conditions, and reconciliation steps.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect a versioned runbook containing detection, authority, fencing, promotion, endpoint/secret rotation, pool draining, verification, return-to-service, stop conditions, and owner assignments. Execute it in a drill and compare each recorded command and timing with the documented procedure.

nodes.title: Failover Drill
nodes.summary: Exercise planned and unplanned failover on a fixed cadence while measuring recovery time, recovery-point loss, lag, retry behavior, and reconciliation. This validates automation and application assumptions under incident conditions.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect dated planned and unplanned drill records with injected failure, measured RTO/RPO, replica lag, client and worker retry results, fencing evidence, and reconciliation output. Require remediation evidence for every failed threshold.

nodes.title: Split-Brain Fencing
nodes.summary: Require authoritative lease, quorum, provider fencing, or equivalent fail-closed controls that prevent the old writer accepting writes before promotion. Validate writer authority epochs and partition behavior.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the lease/quorum/provider configuration, writer epoch validation, credential/network fencing, fail-closed behavior, and partition drill results. Demonstrate that an isolated or delayed old writer receives a write rejection after promotion.

nodes.title: Transaction Boundary
nodes.summary: Commit all database mutations for a business invariant and its outbox record atomically, keeping external calls outside the commit-critical section. This prevents partial state after process or dependency failure.
nodes.probe: Use a static or transaction-trace probe to assert that the business write and outbox insert share one `BEGIN` and `COMMIT` or framework transaction and that no external call occurs inside the commit-critical section. Kill the process before commit and verify neither record is visible; kill it after commit and verify the relay can deliver.

nodes.title: Transaction Isolation
nodes.summary: Document isolation, lock ordering, and bounded retries for every cross-row invariant or concurrent workflow. This prevents write skew, lost updates, phantoms, and deadlocks without unnecessary serialization.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect concurrency design for each cross-row invariant, including isolation setting, lock order, timeout, retry limit, and documented conflict response. Require a concurrent test or production trace showing behavior under interleavings that could otherwise produce write skew or lost updates.

nodes.title: Idempotent Replay
nodes.summary: Associate retried commands, jobs, migrations, and event consumers with stable idempotency keys or deduplication constraints and deterministic duplicate responses. This prevents at-least-once delivery from duplicating business effects.
nodes.probe: Inspect schemas for a unique idempotency or deduplication key and run the operation twice with the same key, asserting one committed effect and a deterministic response. Repeat concurrently and with the same key but a different payload; the latter must be rejected rather than silently reused.

nodes.title: Transactional Outbox
nodes.summary: Persist each externally published event in the business transaction, then relay committed rows with retries, leases, and observable delivery state. This prevents database commits and message publication from diverging.
nodes.probe: Locate the outbox table, transaction write, relay polling or CDC, retry and backoff logic, and sent or lease state; kill the relay between commit and publish and verify eventual delivery without a duplicate business effect. Kill it after broker publish and verify consumers tolerate the resulting duplicate.

nodes.title: Outbox Delivery Order
nodes.summary: Specify per-aggregate ordering, duplicate handling, poison-message quarantine, and retention or compaction for outbox delivery. This preserves causality without blocking unrelated streams.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect event schema, aggregate sequence, partition key, consumer duplicate/gap behavior, retry/quarantine thresholds, and retention policy. Require evidence from an out-of-order, duplicate, and poison-message exercise showing unrelated aggregates continue to flow.

nodes.title: Database Integrity Constraints
nodes.summary: Enforce structural and business invariants with database constraints rather than relying only on application validation. This protects alternate writers and concurrent operations from impossible state.
nodes.probe: Introspect `pg_constraint` and `information_schema` or the engine equivalent and compare required invariants with migration definitions, failing when a rule exists only in application validation. Attempt invalid null, duplicate, orphan, and check-violating fixtures and require database rejection.

nodes.title: Foreign-Key Delete Semantics
nodes.summary: Choose and test explicit foreign-key delete and update actions, including cascade, restriction, history retention, and anonymization behavior. This prevents orphaning, accidental tenant-wide cascades, and retention violations.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect every foreign key's action, history/privacy rationale, tenant-scope protection, migration, and deletion test evidence. Require a dry-run showing affected row counts and verify that the selected action matches the documented business and legal policy.

nodes.title: Concurrency Invariant
nodes.summary: Resolve uniqueness and allocation races atomically with constraints, locks, or serializable transactions instead of check-then-insert logic. The losing operation receives a deterministic conflict or retryable result.
nodes.probe: Run concurrent writers against each declared invariant and assert exactly one succeeds while the losing transaction returns the documented conflict, then inspect the supporting constraint or lock. Repeat after a client timeout to ensure retry remains safe.

nodes.title: Database Validation
nodes.summary: Validate ranges, enums, precision, temporal relationships, encoding, and currency or unit semantics at the database boundary. This prevents malformed values from reaching reports and downstream systems.
nodes.probe: Enumerate `CHECK`, domain, enum, and precision definitions and execute boundary fixtures for null, minimum or maximum, invalid enum, overflow, timezone, and reversed-interval cases, expecting rejection. Compare the constraints with the domain data contract to find rules enforced only in application code.

nodes.title: Constraint Online Validation
nodes.summary: Introduce constraints compatibly, validate existing rows separately, and make enforcement mandatory only after violations are resolved. This separates legacy cleanup from lock-sensitive schema changes.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the compatibility migration, validation command, violation-remediation evidence, lock/timeouts, and final enforcement migration. Require proof that new writes cannot introduce additional violations during the validation window.

nodes.title: Retention Enforcement
nodes.summary: Assign every dataset a retention duration, deletion trigger, legal-basis or hold behavior, owner, and automated purge mechanism across identifiable copies. This prevents indefinite accumulation and policy drift.
nodes.probe: Present the exact decision: “For each dataset, what retention duration and deletion trigger apply, and how do legal holds override them?” Options: time-after-creation, time-after-last-use, subject/request completion, contract/account closure, or indefinite under named legal hold. Require a named owner, jurisdiction/basis, expiry mechanism, and exception date for each dataset.

nodes.title: GDPR Erasure
nodes.summary: Implement a verified subject-erasure workflow that locates identifiers, deletes or irreversibly anonymizes eligible records, records lawful exceptions, and proves completion across operational copies.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the request authorization, identifier map, sink inventory, deletion/anonymization code, legal-hold handling, retry behavior, and a completed synthetic-subject record. Verify a query across every declared store returns no identifying data or a documented lawful exception.

nodes.title: Deletion Lineage
nodes.summary: Map every personal-data field to replicas, indexes, analytics, logs, exports, queues, and backup expiry with testable propagation and acknowledgement rules. This exposes residual copies during erasure.
nodes.probe: Parse the data-catalog or lineage manifest and run a synthetic subject through deletion, asserting every declared sink receives a tombstone or deletion and no query returns the identifier. Fail on undeclared stores or sinks without an acknowledgement path.

nodes.title: PII Inventory
nodes.summary: Maintain a machine-readable inventory of personal fields, identifiers, purposes, stores, owners, access paths, classification, and retention. This keeps unknown personal-data copies within control and erasure scope.
nodes.probe: Compare the catalog against schema columns, JSON fields, event schemas, and config-selected exports using a repository scanner, failing on unclassified candidate fields. Sample runtime stores and verify each candidate has owner, purpose, access, retention, and erasure metadata.

nodes.title: Data Classification
nodes.summary: Assign each dataset and field an approved sensitivity class with handling rules for access, encryption, replication, logging, backups, exports, and non-production use. Exceptions require owners and expiry dates.
nodes.probe: Present the exact decision: “Which approved sensitivity class applies to each dataset/field, and what handling rules follow?” Options: public; internal; confidential; restricted/sensitive personal, financial, health, credential, or regulated data. Require purpose, owner, access scope, encryption/logging/non-production rules, and a dated exception for ambiguity.

nodes.title: Synthetic Non-Production Data
nodes.summary: Use deterministic synthetic or properly de-identified fixtures in development, CI, staging, and migration rehearsals instead of production PII. This prevents uncontrolled personal-data copies in test paths and artifacts.
nodes.probe: Scan fixtures, snapshots, seed files, and CI artifacts for secret or PII signatures, and verify that every non-production dataset is synthetic or has an approved de-identification record. Fail on live-looking identifiers, production connection references, expired approvals, or artifacts accessible outside the intended environment.

nodes.title: Deterministic Seeds
nodes.summary: Version seed and reference data, make it idempotent and environment-scoped, and separate production bootstrap values from test fixtures. Repeated application must produce stable intended state.
nodes.probe: Provision a clean database, apply migrations and seeds twice, then compare normalized row counts and hashes and assert the second run makes no changes outside an explicit mutable-data list. Run in a non-production environment and verify production-only bootstrap values are not loaded from test fixtures.

nodes.title: Audit Trail
nodes.summary: Record append-only, tamper-resistant audit events for sensitive changes with actor, correlation ID, time, reason, classification, resource, and retention controls. This makes mutations and erasure verifiable.
nodes.probe: The assessor must inspect the audit schema, append-only permissions, transactional coupling, actor/correlation fields, redaction rules, retention, and tamper/access monitoring. Perform a sensitive mutation and verify one complete event is queryable; attempt alteration with the application role and require rejection.

nodes.title: Long-Transaction Guardrails
nodes.summary: Bound statement, lock-wait, and idle-in-transaction time while alerting on sessions, blocked locks, replication slots, and WAL growth. This turns abandoned work into an observable and recoverable condition.
nodes.probe: Query `pg_stat_activity`, `pg_locks`, replication slots, and WAL or replication metrics in a staging load test, failing when configured age, lag, or storage thresholds are exceeded or timeouts are absent. Hold an idle transaction deliberately and verify it is terminated or alerted within the policy window.
